requirements.evidence: Contract largely met: Queues.php declares every listed property/method (Queues.php:26-43, openCreate..revokeAccess) and passes accessQueue/accessGrants scoped via $this->entity->queues()->find (Queues.php:207-214); create derives slug with Str::slug($name) (Queues.php:72) and rename re-derives it (Queues.php:140); domain ValidationException mapped to name/renameName; toggle uses a confirmation modal, not wire:confirm (queues.blade.php:92-111); list rows only wire:click="openQueue(..)" (queues.blade.php:12). Serve: callNext handles null selection, scoped findOrFail, InactiveQueue/NoWaitingTickets notices, AuthorizationException uncaught, rate limit 10/min on success (Serve.php:83-115); waiting list ordered priority desc, issued_at, id, limit 30, hidden unless Gate 'call' (Serve.php:122-145). Members tabs with allowlist (Members.php:68-75) and role=tablist (members.blade.php:6). Routes and nav links added; all lang keys in both locales. Gaps: tampered `mode` makes CallMode::from throw a ValueError (500) instead of being validated (Serve.php:100); issue time printed raw (serve.blade.php:49).

conventions.evidence: Uses the Actions (CreateQueue/UpdateQueue/SetQueueAccess/CallNextTicket) and policies, #[Validate] on name/renameName, CHANGELOG updated. But conventions mandate 'No production code without a test' and the diff ships zero test files; `callableQueues()` is a public helper (Serve.php:51) violating rule 5 (internal methods protected/private); `mode` has no #[Validate] (Serve.php:29); employee callable logic re-implements the policy rule with a raw 'call' string instead of QueuePolicy/QueuePermission (Serve.php:60-68).

security.evidence: All client ids resolved scoped: $this->entity->queues()->findOrFail($id) and $this->entity->memberships()->findOrFail($membershipId) (Queues.php:89,116,165,186-187,194-195; Serve.php:91); authorize on mount and mutating actions; lastCalledTicketId #[Locked] (Serve.php:31); waiting list gated by Gate 'call' (Serve.php:125); output escaped with {{ }}. Gaps: `mode` unvalidated (tamper -> ValueError 500, Serve.php:100); grantAccess/revokeAccess rely only on the action for authorization with no $this->authorize('manageAccess', $queue) (Queues.php:184-198); public callableQueues() is an extra callable endpoint (Serve.php:51), though it is read-only and returns nothing useful to the client.

tests.evidence: No test files in change.diff at all (files touched: CHANGELOG.md, Livewire components, lang, views, routes). No happy-path, validation, unauthorized-call or tamper tests for Queues, Serve or the Members tabs, despite the Livewire definition of done requiring them.

simplicity.evidence: Mostly direct component code reusing Actions and existing <x-label>/<x-input>. However Serve::callableQueues (Serve.php:51-80) hand-rolls role and QueueAccess permission checks that duplicate QueuePolicy::call; closeQueue/openQueue duplicate the same reset block (Queues.php:93-99, 104-110); error mapping loop with immediate break duplicated in create/rename (Queues.php:74-78, 142-146) where ->first() would do.

readability.evidence: Clear names, small methods, view structure mirrors the members page (modals, row buttons). Minor: `foreach ... break` to take the first error, untyped `$id` params, missing return type on callableQueues(), redundant resets in Serve::mount (Serve.php:40-42), inline styles repeated in views.

scope.evidence: Every change serves the task: two components + views, routes, nav links, members tabs, lang keys and CHANGELOG entry. Extra lang keys (queues_save, serve_mode_* etc.) are used by the new views. No unrelated refactors.

issues.explanation: The change adds two Livewire components, routes and a members-page behavior with no Pest tests at all, violating the mandatory TDD rule and the Livewire definition of done (unauthorized-call and tamper tests per action).
Client-writable `mode` is neither validated nor locked; a tampered value makes CallMode::from throw a ValueError (500) instead of a validation error.
callableQueues() is an internal helper but declared public, making it a callable Livewire endpoint contrary to rule 5.
Re-implements the call-permission rule (owner/admin roles, raw 'call' string in QueueAccess permissions) instead of reusing QueuePolicy/QueuePermission, so the UI and domain rules can drift.
grantAccess/revokeAccess do not call $this->authorize('manageAccess', $queue) in the component, relying solely on SetQueueAccess for authorization, unlike the other actions.
Issue time is printed as the raw timestamp rather than a formatted time.
Tab anchors have no href or tabindex, so they are not keyboard-focusable; buttons would be more accessible.
foreach-with-break to pick the first error is awkward; $e->validator->errors()->first() is clearer (same in rename).

review.summary: The change builds the Queues management page, the Serve attendant panel, members tabs, navbar links and both locales, mostly matching the contract with correct entity-scoped id resolution and use of the domain Actions. However it ships no tests whatsoever, which the project's conventions treat as mandatory (including unauthorized and tamper tests for every Livewire action), and leaves the `mode` property unvalidated plus a public helper method; it needs changes before merging.
